15"""gcu400 _sobol_engine_scramble_: aten-faithful GF(2) bit transform via int8 MMA. 

16 

17aten semantics (aten/src/ATen/native/SobolEngineOps.cpp): every state slot is 

18scrambled INDEPENDENTLY - the transform never mixes slots. For dimension d and 

19slot j (bits b of v = sobolstate[d][j], output bits q): 

20 

21 v_new[j] = sum_q 2^q * (sum_b ltm'[29-q][29-b] * bit_b(v[j]) mod 2) 

22 ltm' = ltm with the diagonal FORCED to 1 (fill_(1), overwrite) 

23 bits >= 30 of the input are ignored and the output is always < 2^30 (assign). 

24 

25The previous gcu400/generic kernels instead XOR slots into each other via 

26parity(sum_{k<j} ltm[k][j] * state[k]); that only coincides with aten on the 

27degenerate test subspace (0/1 states + tril ltm) where both sides are the 

28identity. This rewrite matches aten bit-exactly on arbitrary states (0/1 and 

29full 30-bit values, tril and non-tril ltm, 43-case GCU matrix + 300-case CPU 

30mirror against torch._sobol_engine_scramble_). 

31 

32Performance (GCU400): the old kernel ran 30 serial rounds per program, each 

33with a strided (BLOCK_D, 32) ltm load + where + tl.sum reduction + where - 

34roughly 240 serial reduction barriers per program (measured ~0.9-1.1 us per 

35small tl.sum on this part), which dominated the 2.97 ms @ dim=5000 baseline. 

36This kernel has exactly ONE tl.dot + ONE tl.sum per dimension: 

37 

38 * the GF(2) contraction rides the int8 MMA path: Sel[j, b] = bit_b(v[j]) 

39 times At[b, q] = ltm'[29-q][29-b] (loaded through an int32 low-word view), 

40 accumulated in int32, and aten's ``t1 % 2`` becomes ``R & 1`` - exact, 

41 no carries (products are 0/1, sums <= 30). 

42 * the parity bits are repacked with a single last-axis tl.sum 

43 (summands hit disjoint bits, so the int32 sum is carry-free). 

44 * grid = min(dimension, 48) programs with a grid-stride loop over dimensions: 

45 48 concurrent programs is the measured GCU400 sweet spot (empty-kernel 

46 dispatch costs ~0.05 us/program, so per-dimension grids pay a hard 

47 ~255 us floor at dim=5000). 

48 * ltm is read through int32 low words (entries are 0/1); the DRAM lines are 

49 the same either way, so int64/int32/int8 loads measure identically - the 

50 low-word view just halves the lane traffic. 

51 

52Coalescing / occupancy pass (this revision): 

53 * the ltm' tile is now loaded as ``At2[q, b]`` so that the *source-bit* axis 

54 (stride 8 B in the int64 ltm) is the fast axis of the tile. The previous 

55 ``At[b, q]`` layout walked 240 B (one full 30-int64 row) per lane, i.e. one 

56 cache line per lane; the row-major layout makes the 32 lanes of a row land 

57 in ~4 consecutive lines. 

58 * the transpose is folded into the operand build: ``Sel^T[b, j]`` is built 

59 directly from ``v`` with a swapped broadcast, so no ``tl.trans`` is needed. 

60 * ``num_warps=1``: the tiles are 32x32 int8, so one warp already issues the 

61 whole MMA; extra warps only pay barrier/DSM overhead (4 warps 0.757 ms -> 

62 1 warp 0.391 ms at dim=5000). 

63 

64Benchmark (do_bench median, dim = 100/500/1000/5000, num_warps=1): 

6553/165/307/1459 us -> 23/54/91/391 us, arithmetic mean 3.1x on top of the 

66previous rewrite (0.39 ms at dim=5000, i.e. ~3.7x over the MMA rewrite alone). 

67""" 

68 

69import logging 

70 

71import torch 

72import triton 

73import triton.language as tl 

74 

75logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

76 

77MAXBIT = 30 

78 

79# Measured GCU400 concurrency sweet spot for this kernel (see module docstring). 

80_SCRAMBLE_PROGRAMS = 48 

81 

82 

83@triton.jit 

84def sobol_scramble_kernel( 

85 sobolstate_ptr, 

86 ltm_ptr, 

87 dimension, 

88 MAXBIT: tl.constexpr, 

89 NPROG: tl.constexpr, 

90): 

91 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

92 jl = tl.arange(0, 32) # slot lanes (30 valid) 

93 bl = tl.arange(0, 32) # source-bit lanes (30 valid) 

94 ql = tl.arange(0, 32) # output-bit lanes (30 valid) 

95 bm = bl < MAXBIT 

96 jm = jl < MAXBIT 

97 qm = ql < MAXBIT 

98 # ltm entries are {0, 1} int64; read the low 32-bit words (little-endian). 

99 ltm32 = ltm_ptr.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32)) 

100 # Repack weights: acc[j] = sum_q (R & 1) << q. Lanes >= 30 read 0 from the 

101 # masked At tile, so their never-shifted weight receives no set bit. 

102 qsh = tl.where(qm, ql, 0) 

103 qw = 1 << qsh 

104 

105 for dd in range(pid, dimension, NPROG): 

106 # At2[q, b] = ltm'[dd][29-q][29-b]; diagonal (b == q) forced to 1. 

107 # Axis order matters: b has stride 8 B in the int64 ltm, so keeping it 

108 # as the fast axis turns the old "one cache line per lane" pattern into 

109 # consecutive lines per row. 

110 at2 = tl.load( 

111 ltm32 

112 + 2 

113 * ( 

114 dd * (MAXBIT * MAXBIT) 

115 + (29 - ql)[:, None] * MAXBIT 

116 + (29 - bl)[None, :] 

117 ), 

118 mask=qm[:, None] & bm[None, :], 

119 other=0, 

120 ) 

121 at2 = tl.where(ql[:, None] == bl[None, :], 1, at2).to(tl.int8) 

122 v64 = tl.load(sobolstate_ptr + dd * MAXBIT + jl, mask=jm, other=0) 

123 v = (v64 & 0x3FFFFFFF).to(tl.int32) # aten reads only bits 0..29 

124 # Sel^T[b, j] = bit_b(v[j]) built directly with a swapped broadcast, so 

125 # no tl.trans is needed. The MMA accumulates sum_b At2 * Sel^T in int32 

126 # and aten's `t1 % 2` is exactly `R & 1` (products are 0/1, no carries). 

127 sel_t = ((v[None, :] >> bl[:, None]) & 1).to(tl.int8) 

128 r_t = tl.dot(at2, sel_t, out_dtype=tl.int32) 

129 # Disjoint output bits -> the int32 sum over the q axis is carry-free. 

130 acc = tl.sum((r_t & 1) * qw[:, None], axis=0) 

131 tl.store(sobolstate_ptr + dd * MAXBIT + jl, acc.to(tl.int64), mask=jm) 

132 

133 

134def _sobol_engine_scramble_(sobolstate, ltm, dimension): 

135 """Owen scrambling of the Sobol state (per-slot GF(2) bit transform, in place).""" 

136 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME _SOBOL_ENGINE_SCRAMBLE_") 

137 

138 assert ( 

139 sobolstate.dtype == torch.long 

140 ), f"sobolstate must be int64, got {sobolstate.dtype}" 

141 assert ltm.dtype == torch.long, f"ltm must be int64, got {ltm.dtype}" 

142 assert sobolstate.shape == ( 

143 dimension, 

144 MAXBIT, 

145 ), f"sobolstate shape must be ({dimension}, {MAXBIT}), got {sobolstate.shape}" 

146 assert ltm.shape == ( 

147 dimension, 

148 MAXBIT, 

149 MAXBIT, 

150 ), f"ltm shape must be ({dimension}, {MAXBIT}, {MAXBIT}), got {ltm.shape}" 

151 

152 grid = (min(dimension, _SCRAMBLE_PROGRAMS),) 

153 sobol_scramble_kernel[grid]( 

154 sobolstate, 

155 ltm, 

156 dimension, 

157 MAXBIT=MAXBIT, 

158 NPROG=_SCRAMBLE_PROGRAMS, 

159 num_warps=1, 

160 ) 

161 return sobolstate
